correctness.rationale: Exact BFS and set-intersection distance agreement on 190 pairs; two complete face enumerations cover all 2^20 subsets at thresholds 2 and 3; explicit matchings of 120 and 1599 disjoint covering pairs respectively are globally acyclic by full 660/13980 Hasse-incidence topological sorts, leaving (0:1,2:19) and (0:1,3:1) critical cells. Forman therefore yields integral wedges. Other stages follow from graph cycle rank, antipodal cross-polytope boundary and diameter. Independent GF2 reductions corroborate.

Projective planes require each same-side point pair to share a line, which fails for the ten-point Desargues configuration.
Affine-plane structure has q^2 points and q(q+1) lines; there is no q with 10 and 10.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The stronger graph-power and incidence-family statements have inapplicable, mathematically decisive hypotheses. Results on the larger cube or different incidence graphs do not imply Rips homotopy of a proper induced subgraph.

value.rationale: A complete integral homotopy/persistence classification for the canonical distance-transitive Desargues incidence graph is a natural graph-metric topological invariant. Its exceptional 19 two-spheres and three-sphere, followed by an antipodal nine-sphere, are nontrivial topology at successive scales not determined by current general girth or plane-incidence theorems. Finite exhaustive proof is appropriate to this motivated named object; no artificial parameter selection or unproved downstream theorem is claimed.
